name: Kazukuru
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Dunn, Michael & Malcolm Ross. 2007. Is Kazukuru really non-Austronesian? Oceanic Linguistics 46(1): 210-231. doi:10.1353/ol.2007.0018. Open postprint at MPG PuRe: https://pure.mpg.de/rest/items/item_60507_2/component/file_60508/content
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 4.1 Phonology (pp. 218-219) covers only the grapheme values of Waterhouse & Ray's transcription, a five-vowel system, (C)V syllable structure and the r/l distinction; no mention of stress or accent anywhere in the paper (the surviving record does not permit it).

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. & B. D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-72. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kazukuru = comparative list 22 (data taken from Waterhouse & Ray 1931); prose: 'Until the 1920s another Papuan language, Kazukuru, was spoken on New Georgia.. information concerning that language is extremely fragmentary.' Wordlists without stress marks; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A. 1975. The East Papuan Phylum in general. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 783-804. http://sealang.net/archives/pl/pdf/PL-C38.783.pdf
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: pp. 787-788: Kazukuru Family (Kazukuru, Guliguli, Dororo) 'now extinct'; 'the family status of this group is doubtful because of the limited materials available on its members'. Classification only; the chapter's one stress remark concerns Rotokas. Silent for Kazukuru.

sources.citation: Voegelin, C. F. & F. M. Voegelin. 1965. Languages of the World: Indo-Pacific fascicle five. Anthropological Linguistics 7(9) (ERIC microfiche ED010365). https://archive.org/details/micro_IA41153350_0265
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists Kazukuru, Guliguli and Dororo as probably dialects of one (formerly spoken) language; classification only, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Waterhouse, J. H. L. & S. H. Ray. 1931. The Kazukuru language of New Georgia. Man 31 (July), art. 133, pp. 123-126. doi:10.2307/2790039. Open scan: Digital Library of India copy of Man vol. 31, https://archive.org/details/;ernet.dli.2015.69952 (page images n153-n156).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only phonological remark (p.124) gives orthographic values: 'Sounds are written as in Roviana, except that ng is written for the italic n (ng in sing); q is the Roviana q (ngg in finger); b and d are mb and nd as in Roviana.' The c.150-item vocabulary, pronouns, numerals and phrases carry no accent marks. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Lanyon-Orgill, Peter A. 1953. The Papuan languages of the New Georgian Archipelago, Solomon Islands. Journal of Austronesian Studies 1(1): 122-138.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only other primary publication on the Kazukuru group (Guliguli and Dororo wordlists, c. 17 pages); could in principle carry a transcription note on accent, though Dunn & Ross 2007, who used it, report nothing of the kind and question its reliability. Low expected yield.

sources.citation: Waterhouse, J. H. L. manuscript materials on Kazukuru (source of the 1931 Man article), if extant in S. H. Ray papers (SOAS) or Methodist Mission archives.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Any fuller field notes behind the published list would be the only conceivable place a remark on accent could survive; existence unverified.
